newsitem.title: USA: Bear Stearns analyst bullish long-term on PC cos.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns analyst bullish long-term on PC cos.

text.p: Bear Stearns & Co Inc analyst Andrew Neff said the fundamental long-term outlook for personal computer makers remains strong, with unit demand over the next five to 10 years likely to exceed expectations.
In a research note, Neff said the rapid pace of change in the industry is likely to preserve the rapid product replacement cycle currently enjoyed by computer makers.
However, he said the near-term outlook could be bumpy, with third quarter earnings warnings due to start soon.
Among the positive indicators Neff cited were declining component prices, corporate upgrades, improvements to notebook computers, and strong demand for so-called intranet products.
Strong back-to-school demand reports from Compaq Computer Corp and Hewlett-Packard Co also bode well for the fourth quarter, he said.
He also noted comments from Compaq, Intel Corp and several other firms that suggest a pickup in activity may be under way in Europe, a sluggish market for the industry.
Neff's picks in the industry include Compaq and Dell Computer Corp. He also cited International Business Machines Corp, Sun Microsystems Inc and Hewlett-Packard as server market standouts.
Among storage device companies, Neff chose Seagate Technology Inc and Western Digital Corp. In the semiconductor industry he named Intel and Adaptec Inc as top picks.
